evidence.claim: Glendale began with a different name and a railroad dispute.
evidence.quote: Solomon Abraham, the local right-of-way agent, platted the community and named it "Julia" after his wife. After a dispute with Abraham, A. F. Morris, the chief engineer for the railroad, changed the name to "Glendale".

evidence.claim: After construction of the line south from Roseburg in 1881–83, right-of-way agent Solomon Abraham platted the community as Julia, honoring his wife.
evidence.quote: After construction of a railroad line south from Roseburg in 1881–83, Solomon Abraham, the local right-of-way agent, platted the community and named it "Julia" after his wife.

evidence.claim: Chief engineer A. F. Morris changed it to Glendale after a dispute with Abraham.
evidence.quote: After a dispute with Abraham, A. F. Morris, the chief engineer for the railroad, changed the name to "Glendale".

evidence.claim: The post office made that switch between February and August 1883.
evidence.quote: A Julia post office was established in February 1883, and its name was changed to Glendale in August of the same year.
